column3: AI Overclocking will determine the optimum overclocking settings for your system.
On applicable platforms, DDR5 has editable XMP Profiles, allowing for greater user control.

On some platforms and configurations, certain frequency points cannot be characterized and will not appear on the graph. Those Point Voltage Offsets controls will be listed here, where they can be configured and may affect voltage points that are scanned.

Frequencies above certain thresholds cannot be scanned due to the instability those frequencies may cause. Any Point Voltage Controls above that frequency will be listed here for tuning as they can still affect voltage points that are scanned.

These changes are added on top of the Core Voltage and Core Voltage Offset settings. Update the Voltage-Frequency Curve by modifying offsets to the voltage at frequency points provided, or the entire curve, and clicking Apply.

The Selected Point Voltage Offset knob controls the voltage offset at selected frequency points. 

Note: Voltage offsets may be adjusted internally to maintain monotonic behavior. Please refer to the help document to get detailed information on VF Curve, monotonic behavior of VF Points and how to use the controls on this page.

Visualize the default as well as applied Voltage-Frequency Curve of the performance cores by clicking the Scan Default VF Curve button or the Scan Applied VF Curve button.

The Default profile needs to be active to scan the Default VF Curve. 

Please scan the default VF Curve before scanning the applied VF Curve.

When enabled this feature automatically overclocks your processor. It changes core frequencies, power and current limits, and version 2.0 now updates OC TVB values on select systems. If system instability is encountered, the optimizations will be turned off after reboot.
With this feature you are able to view XMP Profiles located on your DDR4 and DDR5 RAM.
